chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman whom her husband divorced three times before consummating the marriage, he said: 'She is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.' This does not contradict the earlier reports which indicated that she becomes free (by one divorce), because the meaning in this hadith is that if he contracted marriage with her and divorced her three times, each time before consummating the marriage, then in this state she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.

key_terms.لَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ: she is not permissible to him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman divorced three times before consummation of marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between reports by distinguishing between a single divorce (which causes separation but allows immediate remarriage) and three distinct divorces before consummation, which trigger the 'Iddah of three divorces' requiring a subsequent marriage to a third party (Zawaj al-Muhill) for finality. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the specific conditions of the divorce count relative to consummation, ensuring the husband's right to remarry is properly regulated through the mechanism of *Nikah al-Muhill*.
